notebooks.title: Compositional Heredity across Growth-Division Regimes
notebooks.summary: Multistable autocatalytic reaction networks exhibit compositional memory, allowing stable states to be maintained across growth-division cycles. This memory is driven by the feedback between chemical kinetics and compartment growth, where stochastic transitions between states act as primitive mutations.
notebooks.findings: Multistable autocatalytic reaction networks can maintain stable heritable compositional states. [peer-4a7ca1fd0abb1acbf57e787b] [peer-20adb242125e297a2c7057ee]
notebooks.limitations: The current model relies on theoretical and abstract simulations; experimental verification in non-templated chemical systems remains sparse.
notebooks.next_questions: What specific experimental setups can isolate compositional states from simple thermal relaxation in minimal protocell systems?

detail.title: Compositional Heredity across Growth-Division Regimes
detail.summary: Multistable autocatalytic reaction networks exhibit compositional memory, allowing stable states to be maintained across growth-division cycles. This memory is driven by the feedback between chemical kinetics and compartment growth, where stochastic transitions between states act as primitive mutations.
